brief: Large tilth_search result sets end with the bare tail "... and N more matches. Narrow with scope." (write_hidden_tail, and the same string in format_search_result_seen and search_multi_symbol_expanded in src/search/mod.rs). An agent then re-queries with a guessed scope, often twice, and the content backend (src/search/content.rs) caps a content search at ten matches whatever the budget. Replace the bare tail with a stable continuation: show hits from distinct files before a second hit from an already shown file, and end the tail with an exact follow-up query (for example the same query with a glob that excludes the shown files, or the next page offset) that returns the omitted matches in one further call. Keep the output within the requested budget and keep the editable-line guarantee for every shown line.

format_raw_result_deferred in src/search/mod.rs passes expand 0 to format_search_result_seen, so a content hit that is one line inside a long function shows only that line, and the agent then issues one or two tilth_read calls for the surrounding code. When a content search has few hits (a sparse result), include bounded enclosing context for each hit: the enclosing definition when it fits in about 40 lines, else a window of lines around the hit with its start and end line numbers. Cap the total extra output by the requested budget, add nothing for dense result sets, and keep every shown line editable with the file tag.

In src/mcp/path_suffix.rs, declaration_name leaves `impl` out of its keyword list on purpose, so a tilth_read path such as `src/lib.rs#impl Foo` or `src/lib.rs#impl Trait for Foo` is parsed as no symbol and the call fails with a not-found error; the agent then retries with another form. Make `path#impl X` resolve to the impl block of X, and `path#impl Trait for X` to the block of that trait impl for X (including generic parameters such as `impl<T> Trait for X<T>`), using the existing outline and symbol lookup. When several blocks match, read the first and list the others. Keep the behavior of every other declaration prefix.

The truncate function in src/budget.rs prefers a cut at the last blank-line boundary ("

") in the body. A numbered read (lines of the form `N:content`) can contain a blank source line near its start, so the cut lands there and leaves zero or one content lines, and the message then says to raise the budget although a large part of the budget was unused. Cut on a numbered-line boundary instead: keep as many whole `N:content` lines as fit in the byte budget, always keep at least one content line when any fits, and report the last kept line number in the truncation message so the next read can start after it. Keep the section-heading preference ("

##") for outlines and prose.

Add one short, concrete example of a multi-file edit batch to prompts/mcp.md, near the top where the batching guidance sits: one tilth_search call over several symbols, then one tilth_write call whose `edits` array holds sections for three different files, each section using the tag shown in the search result, followed by no re-read because the receipt returns the new tags. Show it as a tool-call pattern, not prose, in at most six lines. Do not add other text; remove an equal number of bytes elsewhere so the file stays under its size cap.
